chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Hisham ibn Salim and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Miskan, all together from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who struck another man with a staff and did not stop striking him until he was killed: should he be handed over to the heirs of the slain? He said: “Yes, but he is not to be left for them to abuse; rather, the prescribed retribution is to be carried out against him.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ: the legal heirs or avengers entitled to claim qisas
key_terms.بِعَصًا: with a staff or stick used as the instrument of ضرب
key_terms.قُتِلَ: was killed as the result of the assault
key_terms.يَعْبَثُ: to mistreat, abuse, or mutilate beyond lawful punishment
key_terms.يُجَازُ: the legal retribution is carried out against him

ai.seo_question: If a man kills another by repeatedly beating him with a staff, can he be handed over to the victim’s heirs for qisas?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning a killing caused by repeated beating with a staff. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام affirms that the killer may be handed over for qisas, but not in a manner that permits mutilation or abuse; rather, lawful retribution is to be executed in a regulated manner.
